title: Reporting Beliefs and Expectations
summary: Report claims without naming a source using it is said that or a passive reporting verb followed by an infinitive. Choose infinitive forms to show when an event happened, and distinguish hearsay from intended arrangements and restrictions expressed with supposed to.
learningObjectives: Convert an impersonal report into a subject-focused passive reporting construction and back again.
Choose to do, to be doing and to have done to place reported events in time.
Use there is said to be and passive perfect infinitives for appropriate reported claims.
Distinguish supposed to as hearsay, an intended arrangement, an unfulfilled plan or a restriction.

explanation.heading: Report a claim without naming the source
explanation.body: News and conversation often present information as a claim rather than a confirmed fact. One common form is It + passive reporting verb + that-clause. Verbs such as say, believe, report, think, expect and allege can be used this way. A reporting form identifies what is being claimed; it does not prove that the claim is correct.
explanation.example: It is reported that the coastal road will close for repairs.

explanation.heading: Make the subject of the claim the subject of the sentence
explanation.body: When the reported fact has a suitable subject, put that subject first, followed by be + a past participle such as believed, said, known or expected + a to-infinitive. The passive reporting verb agrees with the new subject: the actor is said, but the actors are said. This form is common in factual-sounding reports.
explanation.example: Several paintings are believed to belong to the same collection.

explanation.heading: Choose the infinitive to show time and progress
explanation.body: Use to + base verb for a reported present state, habit or expected future event. Use to be + -ing for an activity believed to be happening. Use to have + past participle for an earlier event; if the earlier event itself was passive, use to have been + past participle. The reporting verb can be present even when the reported event happened years ago.
explanation.example: The researcher is thought to have discovered the letter decades ago.

explanation.heading: Report the existence of something
explanation.body: A claim beginning with there is or there are can become There is said or believed to be + noun phrase. Keep there as the grammatical subject rather than incorrectly making the noun follow a personal reporting verb. This is useful when the main information is that something exists.
explanation.example: There is believed to be a spring beneath the old library.

explanation.heading: Use supposed to for hearsay or reputation
explanation.body: Be supposed to can mean that people generally say or believe something: a café is supposed to be excellent, or an object is supposed to have belonged to someone famous. As with other reporting forms, a perfect infinitive points to an earlier event. Context tells you whether this is a rumour rather than a rule.
explanation.example: The manuscript is supposed to have belonged to a nineteenth-century collector.

explanation.heading: Use supposed to for arrangements and restrictions
explanation.body: Be supposed to also describes what is expected, planned or intended, whether or not it happens. Was or were supposed to + verb often describes a missed or changed arrangement. Not supposed to + verb tells someone that an action is prohibited or discouraged, depending on the context; it does not simply mean that the action is unlikely.
explanation.example: We were supposed to receive the keys on Monday, but the handover was delayed.

comparisons.title: Two ways to report the same belief

left.label: Impersonal claim
left.example: It is believed that the sculpture is genuine.
left.note: The belief is presented using an it + that-clause.

right.label: Subject-focused report
right.example: The sculpture is believed to be genuine.
right.note: The sculpture becomes the subject before the reporting passive.

comparisons.title: Reported activity now versus earlier event

left.label: Ongoing activity
left.example: The crew are reported to be filming nearby.
left.note: To be filming places the activity in progress.

right.label: Earlier event
right.example: The crew are reported to have filmed nearby.
right.note: To have filmed places the activity before the current report.

left.label: Hearsay
left.example: The restaurant is supposed to be very quiet.
left.note: Someone has described its reputation; it might be inaccurate.

right.label: Expected arrangement
right.example: The restaurant is supposed to open at noon.
right.note: There is a planned opening time, whether or not it is met.

examples.sentence: The missing archive is believed to be in a private home.
examples.note: Is believed to be expresses an unconfirmed present location.

examples.sentence: It is alleged that the firm ignored several safety warnings.
examples.note: Alleged marks a claim that has not been established as fact.

examples.sentence: The singer is reported to be recovering at home.
examples.note: To be recovering describes an ongoing situation.

examples.sentence: The bridge is thought to have been damaged during the storm.
examples.note: To have been damaged reports an earlier passive event.

examples.sentence: There is said to be a small observatory on the island.
examples.note: There is said to be reports the claimed existence of something.

examples.sentence: You are not supposed to leave bags beside the emergency door.
examples.note: Not supposed to expresses a restriction.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The actress is believed be living abroad.
commonMistakes.correct: The actress is believed to be living abroad.
commonMistakes.why: The reporting passive requires a to-infinitive; an ongoing action takes to be + -ing.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The ship is thought to sink in the storm last year.
commonMistakes.correct: The ship is thought to have sunk in the storm last year.
commonMistakes.why: Use a perfect infinitive for an event completed before the current report.

commonMistakes.incorrect: There is said a secret passage beneath the theatre.
commonMistakes.correct: There is said to be a secret passage beneath the theatre.
commonMistakes.why: An existential reported construction needs to be after is said.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We were supposed meet at the café at eight.
commonMistakes.correct: We were supposed to meet at the café at eight.
commonMistakes.why: Be supposed is followed by to + the base verb.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Visitors are not supposed using this entrance.
commonMistakes.correct: Visitors are not supposed to use this entrance.
commonMistakes.why: Use to + base verb after supposed, even in a negative rule.

studyTips: When reading reports, underline the reporting verb and decide whether the statement describes evidence, a claim or an expectation.
Rewrite each It is reported that sentence as a subject + is/are reported + infinitive sentence; then check when the reported event happened.
For every supposed to sentence, ask: Is this a rumour, a plan, or a rule? The context changes the meaning.

exercises.prompt: According to local newspapers, the missing painting ___ in a private collection. (A current belief)
exercises.feedback: A subject-focused present belief takes is believed to be; believes is active and to be is required.

exercises.prompt: Experts think the ship sank decades ago. The ship ___ decades ago.
exercises.feedback: To have sunk places the alleged sinking before the present belief.

exercises.prompt: The conference began an hour late. According to the schedule, the first session ___ at nine.
exercises.feedback: Was supposed to begin describes an earlier scheduled event, even though the actual start was late.

exercises.prompt: A staff-only notice is displayed at this door. Visitors ___ enter without permission.
exercises.feedback: A rule preventing entry is expressed with aren't supposed to + base verb.

exercises.prompt: According to news reports, the residents ___ (report / wait) for temporary housing right now. Use a subject-focused reporting passive with a continuous infinitive.
acceptedAnswers: are reported to be waiting
exercises.feedback: The plural subject takes are reported, and to be waiting describes an activity still in progress.

exercises.prompt: Experts believe the bridge collapsed in 1985. The bridge ___ (believe / collapse) in 1985. Use the subject-focused reporting passive.
acceptedAnswers: is believed to have collapsed
exercises.feedback: Is believed reports a current belief, while to have collapsed places the collapse in the past.

exercises.prompt: Local historians say that there is an old tunnel under the square. ___ an old tunnel under the square. Begin with There and use said to.
acceptedAnswers: There is said to be
exercises.feedback: There is said to be introduces the reported existence of a tunnel.

exercises.prompt: The group arranged to meet at noon, but nobody arrived until one. They ___ (supposed / arrive) at noon. Use the past expected-arrangement form.
acceptedAnswers: were supposed to arrive
exercises.feedback: Were supposed to arrive states the plan, not what actually happened.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The actress is believed be living abroad.
acceptedAnswers: The actress is believed to be living abroad.
exercises.feedback: A reporting passive followed by an ongoing activity requires to be living.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: It reported that the museum will reopen in spring.
acceptedAnswers: It is reported that the museum will reopen in spring.
exercises.feedback: The impersonal reporting construction requires is before the past participle reported.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The documents are believed to have stole last week.
acceptedAnswers: The documents are believed to have been stolen last week.
exercises.feedback: The documents received the action; an earlier passive event requires to have been + past participle.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We were supposed call the supplier yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: We were supposed to call the supplier yesterday.
exercises.feedback: Be supposed must be followed by to and the base verb.

speakingExercises.prompt: Journalists say that the actor lives in Madrid. Report this claim in one sentence beginning “The actor” and using “is said” followed by an infinitive.
acceptedAnswers: The actor is said to live in Madrid.
speakingExercises.feedback: Is said to live reports a present situation without identifying the source.

speakingExercises.prompt: Researchers believe that the cave contains ancient paintings. Rephrase as one sentence beginning “It is believed” and include “that”.
acceptedAnswers: It is believed that the cave contains ancient paintings.
speakingExercises.feedback: It is believed that introduces a reported claim using an impersonal passive.

speakingExercises.prompt: People think that the pilot landed safely yesterday. Begin “The pilot” and use “is thought” with a perfect infinitive.
acceptedAnswers: The pilot is thought to have landed safely yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: To have landed correctly puts the reported landing before the current belief.

speakingExercises.prompt: Witnesses report that the workers are repairing the path right now. Begin “The workers” and use “are reported” with a continuous infinitive.
acceptedAnswers: The workers are reported to be repairing the path right now.
speakingExercises.feedback: Are reported to be repairing describes an activity believed to be ongoing.

speakingExercises.prompt: Local people say there is a rare bird on the island. Start with “There” and express this hearsay using “said to”.
acceptedAnswers: There is said to be a rare bird on the island.
speakingExercises.feedback: There is said to be reports the alleged existence of the bird.

speakingExercises.prompt: The bus was scheduled to leave at seven, but it departed at eight. State its planned departure, beginning “The bus” and using “was supposed to”. End with “at seven”.
acceptedAnswers: The bus was supposed to leave at seven.
speakingExercises.feedback: Was supposed to leave describes the original timetable, not the actual departure.

speakingExercises.prompt: This laboratory is restricted. Tell a visitor the rule in one sentence beginning “You”, using “not supposed to” and ending “this laboratory”.
acceptedAnswers: You are not supposed to enter this laboratory.
You're not supposed to enter this laboratory.
speakingExercises.feedback: Not supposed to enter expresses a restriction, not uncertainty.

speakingExercises.prompt: A report claims that the museum sold its oldest sculpture. The museum was also scheduled to open at ten but opened late. Produce exactly two sentences: first begin “The museum” and use “is reported” with a perfect infinitive; second begin “It” and use “was supposed to”.
acceptedAnswers: The museum is reported to have sold its oldest sculpture. It was supposed to open at ten.
speakingExercises.feedback: The first sentence reports an earlier event; the second expresses a missed opening arrangement.

listeningExercises.audioText: The monument is believed to be older than the town itself, but nobody has confirmed its age.
listeningExercises.prompt: What is the status of the monument’s reported age?
listeningExercises.feedback: Is believed and nobody has confirmed mark an unverified claim, not an established fact.

listeningExercises.audioText: The composer is reported to have left the country last Thursday, and she is not expected back until next month.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which timeline does the report describe?
choices: She will leave next month and return on Thursday.
She left today and returned last month.
She reportedly left last Thursday and may return next month.
listeningExercises.feedback: To have left describes a reported earlier action; is not expected back until next month concerns the future.

listeningExercises.audioText: It is believed that the island once had a large forest.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word passive reporting phrase at the start of the recording.
acceptedAnswers: It is believed
listeningExercises.feedback: It is believed introduces the content as a belief rather than a certain fact.

listeningExercises.audioText: Our train was supposed to depart at six, but a signal failure kept us at the station until half past seven.
listeningExercises.feedback: Was supposed to depart describes the plan; the later time shows a delay.

listeningExercises.audioText: This guidebook is supposed to be excellent, though I have never actually read it.
listeningExercises.prompt: Why is the speaker describing the guidebook as excellent?
listeningExercises.feedback: Supposed to be expresses hearsay; the speaker explicitly lacks personal experience.

listeningExercises.audioText: Visitors are not supposed to use the emergency exit unless there is a fire.
listeningExercises.prompt: When is using the emergency exit allowed?
choices: In the event of a fire.
listeningExercises.feedback: The restriction has an explicit exception: unless there is a fire.

listeningExercises.audioText: The singer is thought to have cancelled the tour for personal reasons.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the five-word reporting verb phrase immediately after “The singer”.
acceptedAnswers: is thought to have cancelled
listeningExercises.feedback: The perfect infinitive to have cancelled places the claimed cancellation before the present thought.

listeningExercises.audioText: You are not supposed to leave personal items in this room.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the four words immediately after “You”.
acceptedAnswers: are not supposed to
listeningExercises.feedback: Are not supposed to introduces a restriction.
